claims.text: Machine-learning-based optimization of processing parameters can identify sintering conditions that provide sufficient densification at lower temperatures than conventional sintering.
Powder-based ceramics or metal powders are typically processed using high-temperature sintering.
A predictive model trained on experimental or simulated sintering data can determine processing conditions that lower the required sintering temperature while maintaining densification.
Temperature, heating rate, and dwell time are relevant parameters for optimizing sintering.
Porosity evolution and grain growth characterize densification kinetics and pore closure during sintering.
A machine-learning model can capture nonlinear relationships between sintering parameters and densification behavior.
Historical and simulated data can be used to identify a lower-temperature regime in which liquid- or solid-state diffusion is sufficient for effective particle bonding.
Machine-learning-optimized sintering can reduce sintering temperature by roughly 10–20% relative to conventional processing.
Materials sintered under machine-learning-predicted lower-temperature conditions can retain similar or acceptable densification.
Materials sintered under machine-learning-predicted lower-temperature conditions can retain acceptable strength and low residual porosity.
The proposed approach requires ample sintering data for the target material.
The approach is most applicable when densification is predominantly governed by temperature-dependent diffusion.
Materials with complex reactions or phase evolution during sintering may not follow the trends predicted by the proposed model.
The achievable temperature reduction and performance gains will vary across material systems.
